title: Prawn Bisque
subtitle: Rich, smooth French prawn soup
excerpt: A smooth, velvety prawn soup made from the shells as well as the flesh, with a base of onion, carrot, and celery and finished with double cream. This takes more time than a simple soup but the depth of flavour is worth it.
sourceNotes: Bisque is a classic French cream soup traditionally made from shellfish, with the distinctive technique of roasting the shells to extract maximum flavour before simmering them in a stock. The name bisque dates to 17th century French cookery and has been associated with lobster, crab, and prawn soups ever since.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The bisque base can be made up to 2 days ahead without the cream. Reheat and add the cream just before serving.

content.text: Do not discard the shells. Frying them in butter before making the stock is what gives this bisque its deep, rounded flavour. The shells do most of the work.

Melt the butter in the stockpot over high heat. Add the reserved prawn shells and fry for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until they turn pink and smell fragrant. Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute more.

Add the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 5 minutes. Add 1 litre of water, the bay leaves, thyme, paprika, and chilli flakes. Bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes.

Remove the bay leaves and thyme. Transfer the contents of the pot to the blender jug in batches and blend until smooth. Pass through a fine sieve back into the pot, pressing on the solids to extract all the liquid. Discard the solids.
Return the soup to a gentle simmer. Add the peeled prawns and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until just pink. Pour in the cream, stir, and season generously with salt and pepper. Do not boil.
Ladle into warm bowls and finish with chopped parsley.

items.cause: Not sieved or sieve not fine enough
items.fix: Pass through the finest sieve you have and press hard on the solids.

items.cause: Shells were not fried long enough before making the stock
items.fix: Fry shells until they are bright red and smell sweet before adding liquid.

items.cause: Soup was boiling when cream was added
items.fix: Reduce heat to a bare simmer before stirring in the cream.
